review.notes:
Spoonjoy is the free native iPhone and iPad app for spoonjoy.app. Sign-in is required because recipes, cookbooks, cook logs and shopping lists live in the user's Spoonjoy account and sync with the website.

What makes Spoonjoy different from other recipe managers: every published recipe is a public page on spoonjoy.app (the Share button produces a link anyone can open); recipes can be forked with a permanent "forked from" credit to the original chef; each recipe shows Cooks, which are photo logs from everyone who cooked it; cook-mode progress (current step, scale, checked ingredients) syncs with the server, so it continues on another device or the website; and users can connect an AI assistant through Spoonjoy's MCP connector with OAuth access they can disconnect in Settings → Connections. There are no in-app purchases.

New in 1.2:
- Cook mode: open a recipe, tap Cook. One step fills the screen; on iPhone swipe to change step, on iPad use Back and Next. Close returns to where you started.
- Voice: in cook mode tap the mic, say "next", "back" or "repeat".
- Timer: check a timed step's last ingredient and its timer starts; it shows in the Dynamic Island and Lock Screen.
- Kitchen: Add a recipe (+) in the toolbar; Cooking now reopens a cook in progress.
- iPad: cook in two windows; each keeps its own cook.

Sign-in options (Guideline 4.8): Sign in with Apple is the first option on the sign-in screen on iPhone, iPad and Mac, above Continue with Google, Continue with GitHub and the email and password fields.

Demo account: enter the username and password provided in the email and password fields on the sign-in screen. It is Johnny Appleseed's kitchen: seven apple recipes (Honeycrisp Galette, Tarte Tatin, Waldorf Salad and more), the cookbooks "The Orchard" and "One More Thing", a recipe forked from Tim's Test Kitchen, cook logs from Tim, and a shopping list. Sign in with Apple also works and creates a new, empty kitchen.

Where to find key features:
- Fork credit: open "Brown Butter Apple Crumble, with pecans"; the credit line sits under the title. Recipe actions (···) → Fork to try it.
- Cooks: on any recipe, scroll to Cooks; tap Log to add one (optional photo).
- Cook mode and sync: open a recipe → Cook mode, check an ingredient, then open the same recipe on spoonjoy.app (same account) to see the same step and checks. A step with a duration and ingredients starts its timer when its last ingredient is checked; the timer and the current step show on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island.
- Voice: in cook mode, tap the microphone and say "next", "back", "repeat" or "timer". Recognition runs on the device.
- Shopping: Shopping tab; checkoff works offline. Send to Reminders asks for Reminders access so it can avoid duplicates.
- Siri and Shortcuts: "Start cooking in Spoonjoy", "Next step in Spoonjoy".
- AI features: restyling a cover or importing a recipe first shows a consent sheet naming the provider (Google Gemini or OpenAI) and what is sent. It can be turned off in Settings → Safety & privacy.
- Report and block: on any recipe or chef page, ··· → Report… or Block. Reported content is hidden for the reporter at once and reviewed within 24 hours; blocked chefs disappear from feeds, search and notifications. Manage blocks in Settings → Safety & privacy.
- Privacy policy, terms and support: Settings → About.
- Account deletion: Kitchen toolbar → account button → Settings → Delete account.

iPhone Duo: on the inner screen in landscape, a recipe becomes a two-page spread with its gutter on the hinge. Held tall and half-open (tabletop), cook mode splits at the fold: the step above, the checklist and controls below. iPad in landscape shows the same spread.

Contact: ari@spoonjoy.app

en-US.name: Spoonjoy: Recipes & Cookbooks
en-US.subtitle: Recipes, passed hand to hand
en-US.promotionalText: New in 1.2: cook mode rebuilt around one big step. Say "next" with floury hands, and keep the whole cook in the Dynamic Island. On iPhone Duo, it opens like a cookbook.
en-US.description:
Recipes have always been passed hand to hand: a card in a grandmother's writing, a friend's note in the margin, "less sugar" scribbled after the third try. Spoonjoy is a home for recipes like that. Every recipe has its own page, every version keeps credit to the cook who started it, and every cook leaves a photo and a note for the next person.

Then Spoonjoy helps you cook. Cook mode takes you one step at a time with only the ingredients that step needs, and it follows you from iPhone to iPad to the web.

FORK IT, WITH CREDIT
Like another cook's recipe? Fork it into your kitchen and make it yours. Your version keeps a "forked from" line back to the original chef and recipe, so the credit travels with it.

COOKED BY REAL PEOPLE
Every recipe shows its cooks: who made it, what they changed, what they'd do next time, and a photo. Log your own in a few taps, and turn a great cook photo into the recipe's cover.

RECIPES WITH A HOME ON THE WEB
Every recipe you publish has its own link on spoonjoy.app, and every chef has a kitchen page. Share a recipe and the link opens for anyone, with or without the app.

ONE BIG STEP AT A TIME
Cook mode shows one big step with just what that step needs. Hands covered in flour? Say "next", "back", "repeat" or "timer". The mic listens only while cook mode is open, and speech is recognized on your device. Your step, scaling and checked ingredients sync, so you can start on iPhone and carry on on iPad or the web. The screen stays awake while you cook, in a warm dark mode for night cooking.

A TIMER THAT STARTS ITSELF
Check off a timed step's ingredients and its timer starts on its own. The countdown and your place in the recipe stay on your Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, so the whole cook is a glance away.

A SHOPPING LIST THAT WORKS LIKE A RECEIPT
Add a recipe's ingredients in one tap. Big check targets, aisle filters, and checkoff that keeps working offline. Prefer Reminders? Send a recipe or your whole list to the Reminders list you choose, without duplicates.

COOKBOOKS YOU SHAPE
Save any recipe to your own cookbooks and browse them as a shelf.

BUILT FOR iPHONE, iPAD AND iPHONE DUO
- On iPhone Duo, cook mode follows the hinge. Open flat, a recipe is a two-page spread with its gutter on the hinge: ingredients on the left, method on the right, and steps turn like pages. Stand it half-open and cook mode splits at the fold, the step facing you and the checklist on the counter. iPad in landscape gets the same spread.
- Siri and Shortcuts: "Start cooking in Spoonjoy", "Next step in Spoonjoy", "Start the step timer in Spoonjoy", "Read the step in Spoonjoy", "Continue cooking in Spoonjoy", "Add to my Spoonjoy shopping list".
- Spotlight finds your recipes, cookbooks and shopping items.
- Save a recipe link from Shortcuts or your AI assistant, and Spoonjoy imports it.

YOUR KITCHEN, YOUR CONTROL
Use the same account as spoonjoy.app: sign in with Apple, Google, GitHub or a Spoonjoy password. Connect an AI assistant to your kitchen with access you approve and can revoke. Report a recipe or block a chef from any recipe or kitchen page. Download your data or delete your account at any time. No ads, no subscriptions.

Recipes, cookbooks and cook logs you publish are public. Your email, shopping list and sign-in methods stay private.

Privacy policy: https://spoonjoy.app/privacy
Terms of service: https://spoonjoy.app/terms
en-US.whatsNew:
THE INCIDENT AT STEP FOUR

The butter was browning. The garlic was one breath from burning. Your hands were covered in flour, the recipe was two scrolls away, and the screen had just dimmed. You have lived this. Spoonjoy 1.2 is what we built so you never live it again.

• Cook mode, rebuilt around one big step. Tap Cook and the recipe grows into cook mode; on iPhone, swipe to turn the page; close it and you land right back where you started.
• Say "next". Floury hands? Say "next", "back" or "repeat" and cook mode keeps up. Speech is recognized on your device.
• One timer ring that starts itself. Check off a timed step's last ingredient and its timer sweeps into motion.
• Your whole cook in the Dynamic Island and on the Lock Screen, with the soonest timers first.
• A warm dark mode for cooking at night, glowing amber instead of glaring white.
• Real Liquid Glass, and the same typefaces, brass and paper as spoonjoy.app.
• A rebuilt Kitchen: one "Add a recipe" button, and a Cooking now strip that takes you straight back to the cook in progress.
• Redesigned recipe pages: covers zoom into the page, and long titles and chef names wrap instead of trailing off.
• On iPad, cook in two windows at once.
• On iPhone Duo, cook mode and recipes follow the hinge.
• Sign in with Apple now comes first.

The garlic made it. So will yours.
